clue.text: Film with game of chance including Eva in the cast — name?

indicators.note: to cast metal is to pour it into a new shape, so the words beside it are reshaped
something that includes another thing holds it inside, so the game of chance wraps round the rest

blocks.note: dice is a gambling game
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A quiz question: name the film whose cast includes Eva and which involves a gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is the Bond film Casino Royale, in which Eva Green plays Vesper and dies in Venice, so the surface points straight at the wrong film.
explanation.definitionFit: Death in Venice is the 1971 Visconti film adapted from the Thomas Mann novella.

clue.text: Sounding French she reveals a certain amount of silk, say

definitions.text: a certain amount of silk, say

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word that is pronounced like the French word, not spelt like it

blocks.note: elle is the French pronoun for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman lets a little of her silk garment show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reveals' tempts a solver to look for a hidden word, but it only joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length for measuring cloth, so a quantity of silk could be sold by the ell.

clue.text: Brutal interrogation after which you might call someone a doctor

definitions.text: after which you might call someone a doctor

blocks.note: first meaning: harsh, prolonged questioning of a suspect

blocks.clueFragment: after which you might call someone a doctor
blocks.note: second meaning: the qualification that follows a bachelor's and a master's, namely a doctorate

explanation.walkthrough: Casino Royale features Bond's brutal torture by Le Chiffre. Reading 'call someone a doctor' as summoning medical help after torture is the trap; it means addressing them as Dr.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names harsh questioning, while literally a doctorate is the third academic degree after bachelor's and master's.

clue.text: Man 12 tailed a rebel

indicators.note: to tail something here is to dock its tail, cutting off the final letter

blocks.note: 12 is read as under + cover; cover means insure, and under puts the man beneath it in this down entry
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: An undercover agent was trailed by a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 12 (UNDERCOVER) must be split into 'under cover': the man goes under a shortened word for cover. 'Tailed' looks like 'followed' but means de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is someone who rises in revolt against authority, i.e. a rebel.

clue.text: Service from operative's perspective

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A church service seen through the eyes of a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Vesper Lynd is the Bond girl of Casino Royale, so the agent's view of her fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening service of prayer in the Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Sleep with assistant showing hide that's softened

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off alongside an assistant, revealing a softened hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappa is a soft, supple leather made from sheep or lamb skin, a hide treated to be soft.

clue.text: Greek character has something to bet that needs parking

indicators.note: needs is read as lacks, so the abbreviation for parking is missing from the word

blocks.note: a chip is a casino token you bet with
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A Greek gambler at the casino has a stake but needs somewhere to park.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the 22nd letter of the Greek alphabet, written like an X.

clue.text: Country where card game has gone initially really badly

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

blocks.note: monte, as in three-card monte, is a card game
gone is taken as written; has only joins
the first letter of really

explanation.surface: In this country a game of cards went very wrong for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Casino Royale's high-stakes poker game is set in Montenegro, where it does go badly at first for Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a Balkan country on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: I spy spies regularly on telly, naked …

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the word loses its first and last letters
regularly means taking letters at a fixed interval, every other one starting with the first

blocks.note: telly with its outer letters removed
the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A spy-spotting show on television, broadcast in the nude and trailing off into dots.
explanation.walkthrough: The three dots at the end of the clue are the definition; they are an example of the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the punctuation mark of three dots showing that something is left out or trailing off.

clue.text: I snoop around, a killer that's often drunk

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about and moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy confesses to snooping about, alongside a killer who drinks a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The drunk killer looks like an alcoholic assassin; drunk is meant literally, as poison is swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison is a deadly substance commonly administered in a drink, so a killer that gets drunk.

clue.text: Beat regularly again, reversing administration of 10?

definitions.note: the question mark marks this as a definition by example

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the joined-up letters from back to front

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to drum is to beat in a steady rhythm

explanation.surface: A drummer keeps the beat again and again, then goes into reverse while running something.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is POISON. The backwards form is REDRUM, the word scrawled in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone poison is a way of committing murder, so murder is one example of administering it.

clue.text: In secret, nude knotted on chair with middle cut out around balls

indicators.note: knotted means tangled, so the letters are twisted out of order
cutting out the middle leaves only the two end letters of the word
turned around means facing the other way, so the remaining letters are read back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
chair keeping only its first and last letters
in cricket an over is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A naked figure tied to a chair, a scene from Casino Royale's torture sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Bond tied naked to a cut-out chair in Casino Royale. 'Around balls' looks like a container but 'around' reverses; an over is six deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover describes acting covertly or in disguise, which is the same as doing something in secret.

clue.text: Woman in 1A characters inside club had to appraise

indicators.note: the characters inside a word are its inner letters, with the first and last dropped

blocks.note: Eva is the woman named in the 1 Across clue
the two inner letters of club
to have a meal is to eat, so had = ate

explanation.surface: An actress at a club is having to size something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to assess or judge the worth of something, which is what appraising means.

clue.text: Martini's back on menu a lot — shaken, not stirred

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
shaking something jumbles it up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of Martini
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bond's martini order, shaken not stirred, appears constantly on the drinks menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaken, not stirred' is Bond's famous cocktail order; here 'shaken' is the anagram signal and 'not stirred' the definition, meaning unmoved.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred can mean emotionally moved, so someone not stirred shows no feeling at all.

clue.text: Makers of Bond trailer present Q's successors

blocks.note: a trailer is a short advertisement for a film
present means here, in attendance
R and S follow Q in the alphabet

explanation.surface: The producers of a Bond film's trailer introduce the gadget-master Q's replacements.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is MI6's gadget-maker in the films, but here Q is just a letter and its successors are the next two.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherers are things that stick, and anything that sticks two surfaces together makes a bond.

clue.text: Broccoli perhaps welcomes switching endings for television

indicators.note: switching an ending means the final letter is exchanged for the closing letter of the word named after it

blocks.note: to welcome is to greet
the ending of television

explanation.surface: Bond producer Cubby Broccoli greets a television audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The T before the final S of the welcoming word (the end of its root) is replaced by the end of television. Broccoli recalls Cubby Broccoli, the Bond films' producer, but here it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens is the collective name for leafy green vegetables, of which broccoli is one example.

clue.text: Travel abroad, try banking large bet then perish

indicators.note: banking means storing away, so the word for try holds the abbreviation inside it

blocks.note: a go is an attempt or try
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written
to rot is to decay or perish

explanation.surface: A gambler heads overseas, places a huge stake and ends up dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To globe-trot is to travel widely around the world, particularly in foreign countries.

clue.text: Tedious nonsense making trouble for Pinewood?

definitions.note: question mark: pinewood is read as timber, not the studios

blocks.note: dry means dull or tedious
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A dull, silly film causes problems for Pinewood, the studio where Bond films are made.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinewood Studios near London is where the Bond films are shot, but the definition reads it as wood from pine trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that attacks timber, so it is a serious problem for wood such as pine.

clue.text: Getting the job done but using violence

blocks.note: tho' is a short informal spelling of though, meaning but
rough means violent, as in rough treatment

explanation.surface: Bond finishes the mission, though only by using force.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough means done completely and with attention to every detail, which describes a job fully completed.

clue.text: Back on phone, short airline stocks, ultimately targeting large carrier

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
ultimately points to the last letter of the following word

blocks.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, as is a tot
the final letter of phone
BA is British Airways
the final letter of targeting

explanation.surface: A trader on the phone shorts an airline's shares while targeting a large airline.
explanation.walkthrough: Short, stocks and carrier all suggest finance and airlines; a short is a measure of spirits, and in a down clue the letter goes 'on' (beneath) it. Stocks just means holds next.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote bag is a large open bag for carrying shopping or belongings.

clue.text: Leading double-O M frets about

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: two letter Os
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: M, head of MI6, worries about one of her double-O agents.
explanation.walkthrough: Double-O agents such as 007 have a licence to kill, and M is their boss; here double-O just means two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank or importance, the same as leading.

clue.text: Watch the end!

blocks.note: first meaning: a Swiss watch brand worn by Bond
second meaning: the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a warning to look out for the finale; 'Watch' is a noun naming the wristwatch brand Bond wears in the films.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is a watchmaker's brand and the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so figuratively the end.

clue.text: EON claims director is inventive movie pioneer

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the outer word takes the others inside

blocks.note: taken as written
D is an abbreviation for director
taken as written

explanation.surface: EON Productions, the Bond film company, says its director is an inventive cinema pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: EON Productions makes the Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, a prolific inventor, developed the kinetoscope and early motion-picture cameras, so he pioneered film.

clue.text: Disfigure agent that's turned over winning card

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for agent is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a fed is an American federal agent, as in the FBI
the ace is often the top card

explanation.surface: A scarred agent flips a card at the gaming table to win the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface is to spoil the surface or appearance of something, the same as to disfigure it.

clue.text: Simulate 5 1, say, in toppled lift cage

definitions.note: a verb phrase: act out Vesper's death

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow
toppled means knocked over, so in this down entry the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Restaging the scene in which Vesper drowns in a sinking lift cage in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is VESPERS and 1 is DEATH IN VENICE: in Casino Royale Vesper drowns in a lift cage as a Venetian building collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a scene is to perform or simulate it, so an actor could act Vesper's death in Venice.

clue.text: Check Your Spades James, the writer's title?

blocks.note: to bar is to stop or check
one's is the impersonal possessive, meaning your
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A poker player looks at their spades, like an American asking you to check yours.
explanation.walkthrough: James is not Bond but the crime novelist P. D. James, who sat in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: P. D. James was made a life peer, Baroness James of Holland Park, so her title was Baroness.

clue.text: British security resembling Big Brother? On the contrary

definitions.text: resembling Big Brother? On the contrary

blocks.note: first meaning: the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's MI6

blocks.clueFragment: resembling Big Brother? On the contrary
blocks.note: second meaning: the opposite of a big brother is a little sister

explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother suggests Orwellian state surveillance, which fits secret services, but the contrary of a big brother is a kid sister.
explanation.definitionFit: SIS is the official initialism for MI6, and sis is the informal short form of sister.

clue.text: For Bond, preferring women with funds in hand for poker

blocks.note: straight means heterosexual, which Bond notably is
flush means having plenty of money

explanation.surface: Bond, a womaniser with cash in hand, sits down to play poker.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond wins the Casino Royale game with a straight flush.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight flush is five consecutive cards of one suit, one of the strongest hands in poker.
